title: CMB Spectral Distortions from Resonant Conversions in Atomic Dark Sectors
summary: Dark sectors consisting of atomic constituents (electrons, protons, and photons) offer a well-motivated extension to the Standard Model while providing multiple avenues for phenomenological study. In this work, we explore the impact of conversions between the dark and Standard Model photons in the primordial CMB spectral distortion epoch ($10^3 \lesssim z \lesssim 10^6$). These conversions are resonantly enhanced when the induced thermal masses of both photonic species are equal, thus leading to the possibility that sizeable distortions can be produced. To this end, we solve the Boltzmann equation at early times to determine the (irreducible) freeze-in or freeze-out abundance of dark photons. This procedure also allows us to update the limits on generic milli-charged dark sectors using the ACT DR6 bound on the number of effective radiative degrees of freedom ($N_{\rm eff}$). By then modeling the evolution of the thermal masses in both sectors, we compute the primordial CMB distortion using the Landau-Zener formalism. We find that when the dark electron and proton are roughly similar in mass (the positronium limit), current spectral distortion data from the COBE/FIRAS instrument is able to rule out novel regions of parameter space. We also forecast bounds from the proposed FOSSIL satellite, finding that spectral distortions can also be used to probe the ultra-low dark electric charge regions of parameter space, which are difficult to investigate by other means.

AI.tldr: Dark atomic sectors with photon conversions can produce CMB spectral distortions, enabling new constraints on milli-charged dark matter from COBE/FIRAS data and future FOSSIL satellite observations.
AI.motivation: Dark sectors with atomic constituents (electrons, protons, photons) provide well-motivated extensions to the Standard Model. The paper explores how conversions between dark and Standard Model photons during the primordial CMB spectral distortion epoch (z ~ 10^3-10^6) could produce observable distortions, offering a new probe for dark sector physics.
AI.method: 1) Solve Boltzmann equations at early times to determine freeze-in/freeze-out abundance of dark photons. 2) Model evolution of thermal masses in both sectors. 3) Compute primordial CMB distortions using Landau-Zener formalism for photon conversions resonantly enhanced when thermal masses are equal. 4) Apply this framework to update constraints on milli-charged dark sectors using ACT DR6 bounds on N_eff.
AI.result: 1) Current COBE/FIRAS spectral distortion data rules out novel regions of parameter space when dark electron and proton masses are similar (positronium limit). 2) The method provides updated limits on generic milli-charged dark sectors using ACT DR6 N_eff bounds. 3) Forecasts show the proposed FOSSIL satellite could probe ultra-low dark electric charge regions inaccessible to other methods.
AI.conclusion: Primordial CMB spectral distortions provide a powerful probe of dark atomic sectors with photon conversions. Current data already constrains new parameter space, and future instruments like FOSSIL could extend sensitivity to ultra-low charge regions, complementing other dark matter search strategies.

title: The Signature of Strong High-Redshift Radio Backgrounds on the Cosmic Dawn 21-cm Bispectrum
summary: Measurements from the Absolute Radiometer for Cosmology, Astrophysics, and Diffuse Emission 2 (ARCADE-2) reveal a strong radio background in the GHz frequency range. Since the cosmological 21-cm signal is measured relative to the background radiation temperature, the presence of a radio excess can significantly alter its characteristics. Previous studies have explored the impact of an inhomogeneous radio background on the global 21-cm signal and 21-cm power spectrum. This non-uniform radio background is also expected to introduce substantial non-Gaussianity. In this work, using the bispectrum, we analyze the non-Gaussianity in the 21-cm signal in the presence of an excess galactic radio background and investigate how line-of-sight radio fluctuations from early galaxies influence its nature. We find that even a moderate enhancement in radio efficiency in early galaxies significantly affects the small-scale 21-cm bispectrum. Furthermore, the delayed heating transition caused by a galactic radio background shifts the sign change in the squeezed-limit bispectrum to lower redshifts ($z\sim11$), providing a potential observational signature for distinguishing different radio background models. These results demonstrate that the 21-cm bispectrum, particularly in the squeezed limit, is highly sensitive to radio background fluctuations, making it a powerful tool for probing high-redshift radio-loud sources and the physics of the early cosmic epoch.

AI.tldr: Analysis of 21-cm signal non-Gaussianity using bispectrum reveals sensitivity to radio background fluctuations, with galactic radio background causing delayed heating transition and shifting squeezed-limit bispectrum sign change to z~11.
AI.motivation: The ARCADE-2 measurements show a strong radio background in GHz range, which can significantly alter the cosmological 21-cm signal characteristics. Previous studies explored inhomogeneous radio background effects on global signal and power spectrum, but non-uniform radio background is expected to introduce substantial non-Gaussianity that needs investigation.
AI.method: Using bispectrum analysis to study non-Gaussianity in the 21-cm signal in presence of excess galactic radio background. Investigates how line-of-sight radio fluctuations from early galaxies influence the nature of the signal, focusing on squeezed-limit bispectrum behavior.
AI.result: Moderate enhancement in radio efficiency in early galaxies significantly affects small-scale 21-cm bispectrum. Galactic radio background causes delayed heating transition, shifting sign change in squeezed-limit bispectrum to lower redshifts (z~11), providing potential observational signature for distinguishing different radio background models.
AI.conclusion: The 21-cm bispectrum, particularly in squeezed limit, is highly sensitive to radio background fluctuations, making it a powerful tool for probing high-redshift radio-loud sources and early cosmic epoch physics. The distinctive signature in squeezed-limit bispectrum can help distinguish between different radio background scenarios.

title: The Cosmological Parameters (2025)
comment: 19 pages LaTeX file. Article for The Review of Particle Physics 2026 (aka the Particle Data Book), on-line version at https://pdg.lbl.gov . This article supersedes arXiv:2403.15526 and earlier versions listed there
summary: This is a review article for The Review of Particle Physics 2026 (aka the Particle Data Book), appearing as Chapter 25. It forms a compact review of knowledge of the cosmological parameters near the end of 2025. Topics included are Parametrizing the Universe; Extensions to the standard model; Probes; Bringing observations together; Outlook for the future.

AI.tldr: A review article for the 2026 Particle Data Book summarizing current cosmological parameter knowledge as of late 2025, covering parametrization, beyond-standard-model extensions, observational probes, data synthesis, and future prospects.
AI.motivation: To provide a comprehensive, up-to-date summary of cosmological parameters for the particle physics community, consolidating the latest observational constraints and theoretical developments as a reference resource in the Particle Data Book.
AI.method: Review article methodology: synthesizing and analyzing existing observational data from multiple cosmological probes, theoretical modeling of cosmological parameters, and assessing extensions to the standard cosmological model.
AI.result: A compact review presenting the current state of knowledge on cosmological parameters, including constraints on key parameters like H₀, Ω_m, Ω_Λ, σ₈, and ns, along with assessments of tensions and evidence for beyond-ΛCDM physics.
AI.conclusion: The review provides a snapshot of cosmological understanding as of late 2025, highlighting areas of consensus, remaining tensions, and future observational directions for resolving open questions in cosmology.

title: Constraining Lorentz Violation using 21cm and CMB Cross Correlations
summary: Lorentz symmetry is a fundamental pillar of modern Physics, yet high-energy theories often predict its violation. One potential signature of such a violation is cosmic birefringence - rotation of the polarization plane of photons due to Chern-Simons coupling in Maxwell's electrodynamics. This rotation angle, aka birefringence angle, depends upon the distance travelled by the photon and is thus different for CMB and 21cm photons. While the rotation angle in CMB, i.e., $α_\mathrm{CMB}$, has been tightly constrained by CMB experiments, the potential of the 21cm cosmological signal to constrain this parameter, as well as constrain $α_\mathrm{21cm}$, remains largely unexplored. In this work, we provide constraints on both these angles by cross-correlating 21cm and CMB signals. Using the Fisher matrix formalism, we give our forecasts for 21cm experiments, including SKA, HIRAX, and PUMA, and Planck like CMB experiment. We find that best constraints $σ_{α_\mathrm{CMB}} \sim 4.4^\circ$ and $σ_{α_\mathrm{21cm}} \sim 100^\circ$ are found using $C_\ell^{T_{21} B_\mathrm{CMB}}$ and $C_\ell^{T_{21} B_{21}}$ respectively. Since birefringence hasn't yet been detected in 21cm, we choose the fiducial value $α_\mathrm{21cm}^\mathrm{fid}=0$ assuming the null hypothesis.

AI.tldr: The paper forecasts constraints on cosmic birefringence angles for CMB and 21cm signals using cross-correlation analysis with future experiments.
AI.motivation: Lorentz symmetry violation predicted by high-energy theories could manifest as cosmic birefringence, but constraints on the 21cm birefringence angle remain largely unexplored compared to CMB constraints.
AI.method: Using Fisher matrix formalism to forecast constraints by cross-correlating 21cm and CMB signals from experiments including SKA, HIRAX, PUMA, and Planck-like CMB experiments.
AI.result: Best constraints: σ_α_CMB ∼ 4.4° from Cℓ^{T21 B_CMB} and σ_α_21cm ∼ 100° from Cℓ^{T21 B_21}, with fiducial α_21cm^fid = 0 assuming null hypothesis.
AI.conclusion: Cross-correlation of 21cm and CMB signals provides a promising method to constrain cosmic birefringence angles, offering complementary constraints to CMB-only measurements.

title: Ultramassive Black Holes and the Three $M$-$σ$ Relations
summary: I consider recent observations of ultramassive black holes. These appear to confirm theoretical predictions that the relation between central black hole mass $M$ and spheroid velocity dispersion $σ$ has the same form $M \propto σ^4$ in spiral galaxies, elliptical galaxies, and cluster ellipticals, but has differing normalizations. These arise from the need for longer black hole accretion episodes to expel the gas otherwise potentially able to feed the holes in the latter two types of host. In a sample drawn from a mixture of galaxy host types the fitted power of $σ$ will slightly exceed the theoretically-derived value of 4 because of the differing normalizations. The observed hole masses do not currently reach the theoretical maximum values possible for disc accretion, set by the equality of the ISCO and self-gravity radii, probably because the host galaxies have insufficient gas.

AI.tldr: Observations confirm the M ∝ σ⁴ relation for black holes across galaxy types, but with different normalizations due to varying accretion durations needed to expel gas; fitted exponents slightly exceed 4 in mixed samples, and observed masses don't reach theoretical maxima due to insufficient gas.
AI.motivation: To reconcile recent observations of ultramassive black holes with theoretical predictions about the M-σ relation across different galaxy types, explaining why normalizations differ and why observed masses fall below theoretical maxima.
AI.method: Theoretical analysis of black hole accretion physics, considering the need for longer accretion episodes to expel gas in elliptical galaxies and cluster ellipticals compared to spirals, leading to different normalizations in the M-σ relation.
AI.result: The M ∝ σ⁴ relation holds with the same form across spiral galaxies, elliptical galaxies, and cluster ellipticals, but with differing normalizations; fitted exponents in mixed samples slightly exceed 4 due to these normalization differences; observed hole masses don't reach theoretical maxima set by ISCO and self-gravity radii equality.
AI.conclusion: The observed M-σ relation confirms theoretical predictions with consistent slope but varying normalizations across galaxy types, with current mass limits likely constrained by insufficient gas supply rather than fundamental accretion physics limits.

title: VENUS: Strong-lensing model of MACS J1931.8-2635 -- revealing the farthest multiply imaged supernova
comment: 20 pages, 6 figures, 4 tables; submitted to ApJ
summary: We present a parametric strong-lensing model for the galaxy cluster MACS J1931.8-2635 ($z_l = 0.35$), accompanying the detection of the spectroscopically confirmed SN Eos at $z = 5.13$ (Coulter et al. 2026). We identify 10 new multiple-image systems in recent VENUS JWST/NIRCam imaging, so that the model is constrained with a total of 19 robust multiple-image systems -- nine of which also have a spectroscopic redshift. For the point-like source corresponding to SN Eos, our model predicts a total of five images, with the observed radial image pair having a similar magnification of $μ\simeq 25 - 30$ and a small time delay of $< 5$ days, in agreement with their simultaneous observation. According to the model, the other three predicted images arrived earlier, with time delays of $3.7 \pm 0.7$, $3.5 \pm 0.7$ and $54.0 \pm 10.8$ years prior to the two observed images, and with magnifications of $12.9 \pm 2.6$, $13.0 \pm 2.9$ and $2.2 \pm 0.4$, respectively. The absence of detections at the predicted positions, where the host galaxy's images are also visible, confirms the transient nature of the source. SN Eos and its host galaxy are studied in separate articles, and we here focus on the lens model. The final model reaches a very good $r.m.s.$ distance between model and observations of $0.44''$. We present the lens-modeling results, including newly identified systems such as a triply imaged, grand-design spiral galaxy candidate at $z \simeq 3.65_{-0.09}^{+0.04}$, and briefly discuss the potential of using high-redshift lensed SNe for cosmography.

AI.tldr: Strong-lensing model for galaxy cluster MACS J1931.8-2635 predicts 5 images of SN Eos at z=5.13, with 2 observed and 3 earlier arrivals; model constrained by 19 multiple-image systems including 10 new ones from JWST/NIRCam.
AI.motivation: To develop a precise strong-lensing model for MACS J1931.8-2635 cluster to study the lensed supernova SN Eos at z=5.13 and understand its multiple imaging properties, time delays, and magnifications.
AI.method: Parametric strong-lensing modeling using 19 robust multiple-image systems (including 10 newly identified from VENUS JWST/NIRCam imaging), with 9 having spectroscopic redshifts. Model predicts image positions, magnifications, and time delays for SN Eos.
AI.result: Model predicts 5 total images for SN Eos: 2 observed radial images with μ≈25-30 and <5 day delay, plus 3 earlier arrivals with delays of 3.7±0.7, 3.5±0.7, and 54.0±10.8 years and magnifications of 12.9±2.6, 13.0±2.9, and 2.2±0.4. Model achieves r.m.s. of 0.44". Also identifies triply imaged spiral galaxy candidate at z≈3.65.
AI.conclusion: The lens model successfully explains SN Eos observations and confirms its transient nature through non-detection of predicted earlier images. Demonstrates potential of high-redshift lensed supernovae for cosmography studies.

title: Modeling Globular Cluster Stellar Streams with a Basis-Expansion N-body Code
summary: Globular cluster stellar streams probe galaxy-formation processes and can potentially reveal the distribution of dark matter in galaxies. In many theoretical studies, streams are modeled with particle-spray or direct N-body codes. But particle-spray methods abstract away the internal dynamics of the progenitor by making strong assumptions about the escape physics, while direct N-body is prohibitively expensive for realistic (N>10^5) systems. In this paper, we present the stream-modeling capabilities of KRIOS, a new basis-expansion N-body code for collisional stellar dynamics, that bridges this runtime vs. accuracy gap. We show that KRIOS reproduces NBODY6++GPU cluster models, and their associated streams, more accurately than particle spray in a fraction of the NBODY6++GPU wall-clock time. We then compare KRIOS to various particle-spray methods on 10 orbits similar to known Milky Way streams. The morphology and kinematics of these streams most disagree when the progenitor is tightly bound to the host, as these systems are often subject to stronger tidal forces. Finally, we discuss which elements of the progenitor physics are most important for modeling stellar streams and how these might be incorporated into particle-spray methods.

AI.tldr: KRIOS is a new basis-expansion N-body code that bridges the gap between accurate but expensive direct N-body simulations and fast but oversimplified particle-spray methods for modeling globular cluster stellar streams.
AI.motivation: Current methods for modeling globular cluster stellar streams have limitations: particle-spray methods oversimplify progenitor internal dynamics with strong assumptions about escape physics, while direct N-body methods are computationally prohibitive for realistic systems (N>10^5). There's a need for a method that balances accuracy and computational efficiency.
AI.method: KRIOS, a new basis-expansion N-body code for collisional stellar dynamics, is presented. It uses basis expansion techniques to efficiently model stellar systems while maintaining physical accuracy. The method is validated against NBODY6++GPU cluster models and compared to various particle-spray methods on 10 orbits similar to known Milky Way streams.
AI.result: KRIOS reproduces NBODY6++GPU cluster models and their associated streams more accurately than particle-spray methods in a fraction of the wall-clock time. Stream morphology and kinematics show the greatest disagreement between methods when progenitors are tightly bound to the host galaxy, as these systems experience stronger tidal forces. The study identifies which elements of progenitor physics are most important for accurate stream modeling.
AI.conclusion: KRIOS successfully bridges the runtime vs. accuracy gap in stellar stream modeling. The code provides a more physically accurate alternative to particle-spray methods while remaining computationally feasible compared to direct N-body simulations. The research also provides insights into how particle-spray methods could be improved by incorporating key elements of progenitor physics identified in the study.

title: Gravitational waves from supercooled phase transitions and pulsar timing array signals
summary: The recent detection of a gravitational wave background in the nano-Hertz frequency range by Pulsar Timing Array (PTA) collaborations, including NANOGrav, EPTA, and PPTA, has opened a new avenue for exploring fundamental physics in the early universe. In this work, we analyze a supercooled first-order phase transition in a hidden sector with a spontaneously broken $U(1)_X$ gauge symmetry as a source for this signal. We demonstrate that the thermal history of the hidden and visible sectors plays a crucial role in the gravitational wave power spectrum analysis. Our analysis shows that supercooled phase transitions can generate gravitational waves strong enough to explain the PTA observations while satisfying cosmological constraints from Big Bang Nucleosynthesis.

AI.tldr: Supercooled first-order phase transition in hidden sector with broken U(1)_X gauge symmetry can explain nano-Hertz gravitational wave background detected by PTAs while satisfying BBN constraints.
AI.motivation: Recent detection of nano-Hertz gravitational wave background by PTA collaborations (NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA) provides new opportunity to explore early universe physics; need to identify viable sources for this signal.
AI.method: Analyze supercooled first-order phase transition in hidden sector with spontaneously broken U(1)_X gauge symmetry; incorporate thermal history of both hidden and visible sectors in gravitational wave power spectrum analysis.
AI.result: Supercooled phase transitions can generate gravitational waves strong enough to explain PTA observations while satisfying cosmological constraints from Big Bang Nucleosynthesis (BBN).
AI.conclusion: Hidden sector supercooled first-order phase transitions provide viable explanation for nano-Hertz gravitational wave background detected by PTAs, with thermal history playing crucial role in analysis.

title: Quintessence with tachyonic resonance and late-time cosmic-microwave-background and gravitational-wave signals
summary: Combinations of recent cosmological observations, including Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), show hints of a dynamical nature for dark energy. While the data suggest the possibility of the phantom crossing, it is worth thoroughly exploring quintessence models. Given that phenomenological parametrisations of the equation-of-state parameter $w(a)$ with a sharp transitional feature fit the data well, we study the realisation of such models in quintessence. In the late Universe, the quintessence field begins to oscillate abruptly, changing the behaviour of $w$. Naturally, such a model entails tachyonic instability, and particle production modifies $w$. We perform numerical lattice simulations to study the time dependence of $w$. In addition, the violent particle production produces significant density perturbations and the stochastic gravitational-wave background, whose characteristic scale depends on the mass scale of the quintessence around the minimum of the potential. We discuss the observability of these late-time cosmological signals through cosmic microwave background, quasar astrometry, pulsar timing arrays, and other observational probes.

AI.tldr: Quintessence models with oscillating fields can explain DESI's dynamical dark energy hints, producing phantom crossing, particle production, gravitational waves, and observable cosmological signals.
AI.motivation: Recent cosmological observations (including DESI) suggest dynamical dark energy with possible phantom crossing. Phenomenological parametrizations with sharp transitions fit data well, motivating exploration of quintessence models that can realize such behavior.
AI.method: Study quintessence models where the field begins abrupt oscillations in the late Universe, changing w behavior. Perform numerical lattice simulations to study time dependence of w. Analyze particle production, density perturbations, and gravitational-wave background generation.
AI.result: Quintessence oscillations naturally produce tachyonic instability and particle production that modifies w. Violent particle production generates significant density perturbations and stochastic gravitational-wave background with characteristic scale dependent on quintessence mass around potential minimum.
AI.conclusion: These late-time cosmological signals (density perturbations, gravitational waves) are potentially observable through CMB, quasar astrometry, pulsar timing arrays, and other probes, providing testable predictions for dynamical dark energy models.

title: ARCHITECTS I: Impact of subgrid physics on the simulated properties of the circumgalactic medium
summary: Galaxy evolution is shaped by star formation and stellar feedback at scales unresolved by current high-resolution cosmological simulations. Precise subgrid models are thus necessary, and different approaches have been developed. However, they are degenerate and often primarily calibrated to reproduce stellar masses from observations. To explore these degeneracies, we perform three cosmological zoom-in radiation-hydrodynamics simulations of the same galaxy within a $5\times10^{11}\rm\ M_\odot$ dark matter halo at $z\sim1$, each with a different subgrid model: mechanical feedback, a combination of mechanical feedback and thermal feedback, and delayed cooling. We calibrate the simulations to match in stellar mass, isolating the effect of the models on the circumgalactic medium (CGM). Our findings demonstrate that despite producing galaxies with comparable stellar masses, the three models lead to distinct feedback modes, resulting in notable variations in the CGM properties. The delayed cooling run is dominated by ejective feedback and exhibits high burstiness, whereas mechanical and the hybrid models primarily feature preventive feedback, respectively acting at the galaxy and halo scales. Delayed cooling reduces the baryon mass to half the universal baryon fraction while mechanical feedback retains most baryons, with the hybrid model standing in between. Delayed cooling also ejects significantly more metals into the CGM than both other models. While for delayed cooling and mechanical feedback metals are almost evenly distributed in the CGM, they are concentrated around satellites in the hybrid model. These discrepancies emphasize the need to design an appropriate subgrid model to understand how stellar feedback regulates galaxy growth.

AI.tldr: Three cosmological zoom-in simulations of the same galaxy with different stellar feedback subgrid models (mechanical, mechanical+thermal hybrid, delayed cooling) produce comparable stellar masses but lead to distinct feedback modes and CGM properties.
AI.motivation: To explore degeneracies in stellar feedback subgrid models that are typically calibrated only to match observed stellar masses, and to understand how different feedback implementations affect circumgalactic medium properties despite producing similar stellar masses.
AI.method: Three cosmological zoom-in radiation-hydrodynamics simulations of the same galaxy within a 5×10¹¹ M⊙ dark matter halo at z∼1, each with different subgrid models: (1) mechanical feedback, (2) mechanical+thermal hybrid feedback, and (3) delayed cooling. All models were calibrated to match stellar mass.
AI.result: Despite producing galaxies with comparable stellar masses, the three models lead to distinct feedback modes: delayed cooling shows ejective feedback with high burstiness; mechanical and hybrid models show preventive feedback at galaxy and halo scales respectively. Delayed cooling reduces baryon mass to half universal fraction while mechanical retains most baryons. Delayed cooling ejects significantly more metals into CGM, with different spatial distributions across models.
AI.conclusion: Different stellar feedback subgrid models, even when calibrated to produce similar stellar masses, lead to significantly different CGM properties and feedback modes, emphasizing the need for appropriate subgrid model design to understand how stellar feedback regulates galaxy growth.

title: Zel'dovich smearing approximation of the BAO feature for model-agnostic cosmological inference
comment: 33 pages (13 + Appendices), 8 figures, prepared for submission to JCAP
summary: A model-agnostic description of the baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) feature in redshift space requires a number of ingredients. Physically, one must describe the impact of cosmological bulk flows which progressively and anisotropically smear out the feature over time. One must also model the effects of the scale dependence of tracer bias and the mode coupling between short and long scales. All of these can be incorporated using the Zel'dovich approximation alone, without reference to any particular cosmological model. On the technical front, one needs a robust, complete and cosmology-independent basis to describe the shape of the real space BAO feature in linear theory, which can then be propagated to the nonlinearly evolved, measured feature in redshift space. In this work, we describe how these ingredients -- which we have systematically constructed in recent work -- come together in an accurate framework capable of describing the BAO-scale pairwise measurements of state-of-the-art galaxy surveys. Using mock observations and $N$-body simulations, we show that our template-free framework can produce unbiased and precise cosmological constraints for samples with realistic levels of nonlinearity. This work represents one of the final steps in constructing a data-ready analysis framework for model-agnostic cosmological inference from the BAO feature.

AI.tldr: A model-agnostic framework for analyzing baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) in redshift space that incorporates physical effects like bulk flows, tracer bias, and mode coupling using Zel'dovich approximation, enabling unbiased cosmological constraints without reference to specific cosmological models.
AI.motivation: To develop a complete, model-agnostic description of BAO features in redshift space that can handle realistic nonlinear effects and produce unbiased cosmological constraints for modern galaxy surveys without being tied to specific cosmological models.
AI.method: Uses Zel'dovich approximation to incorporate physical effects (bulk flows, tracer bias, mode coupling) without reference to specific cosmological models. Develops a cosmology-independent basis for describing real-space BAO features in linear theory, then propagates to nonlinear redshift-space measurements. Validates using mock observations and N-body simulations.
AI.result: The framework produces unbiased and precise cosmological constraints for samples with realistic levels of nonlinearity, demonstrating its effectiveness as a data-ready analysis framework for model-agnostic cosmological inference from BAO features.
AI.conclusion: This work represents a final step in constructing a complete, model-agnostic framework for BAO analysis that can handle realistic survey conditions and provide unbiased cosmological constraints independent of specific cosmological models.

title: ARCHITECTS II: Impact of subgrid physics on the observable properties of the circumgalactic medium
summary: Galaxy evolution is driven by star formation and stellar feedback on scales unresolved by current high-resolution cosmological simulations, requiring robust subgrid models. However, these models remain degenerate, often calibrated primarily to match observed stellar masses. To explore these degeneracies, we conduct three state-of-the-art cosmological zoom-in simulations of the same galaxy, each incorporating different subgrid models: mechanical feedback, a combination of mechanical and thermal feedback, and delayed cooling. We compare their circumgalactic media (CGM) through quasar absorption sightlines of HI, MgII, CIV, and OVI. Our findings demonstrate that despite producing galaxies with the same stellar masses, the models lead to distinct feedback modes and CGM properties. Column densities and covering fractions serve as effective diagnostics of subgrid models, with all four ions providing strong constraints as they trace diverse gas phases, exhibit complementary spatial distributions, and originate from different mechanisms. Although all simulations bracket observed column density distributions, direct comparisons are limited by scarce detections and significant scatter in absorption strengths. Covering fractions of weak absorbers provides the most robust constraints. All models fail to reproduce HI and MgII covering fractions, and delayed cooling overproduces OVI covering fractions, while the other models underproduce them. The simulation including mechanical feedback reproduces the observed CIV covering fractions well, whereas the other models show slight offsets. We argue that this discrepancy is likely driven by unresolved thermal structures for HI and MgII, and insufficient metals for CIV and OVI, arising from missing physics such as AGNs or cosmic rays.

AI.tldr: Different subgrid feedback models produce galaxies with similar stellar masses but distinct CGM properties, with absorption line diagnostics effectively constraining model choices, though all models fail to fully match observations due to missing physics.
AI.motivation: To address degeneracies in subgrid feedback models for galaxy evolution, which are typically calibrated only to match stellar masses, by comparing how different models affect circumgalactic medium properties through absorption line diagnostics.
AI.method: Conducted three cosmological zoom-in simulations of the same galaxy with different subgrid models: mechanical feedback, mechanical+thermal feedback, and delayed cooling. Compared CGM properties using quasar absorption sightlines of HI, MgII, CIV, and OVI ions.
AI.result: Despite producing galaxies with identical stellar masses, models led to distinct feedback modes and CGM properties. Column densities and covering fractions effectively diagnose subgrid models. All simulations bracket observed column density distributions but have limitations. All models fail to reproduce HI and MgII covering fractions; delayed cooling overproduces OVI while others underproduce it; mechanical feedback best reproduces CIV covering fractions.
AI.conclusion: Absorption line diagnostics provide strong constraints on subgrid feedback models, but discrepancies with observations suggest missing physics such as unresolved thermal structures, insufficient metals, AGN feedback, or cosmic rays are needed to fully reproduce CGM properties.

title: Multiscale feature integration network for inpainting of full-sky CMB $B$-modes
summary: Foreground masking and incomplete sky coverage complicate CMB polarization analyses by inducing mode coupling and imperfect E/B separation, with particularly strong impact on searches for primordial $B$-modes. We present SkyReconNet-P, a convolutional neural network for inpainting CMB polarization maps that extends the SkyReconNet framework to jointly reconstruct the polarization $(Q,U)$ maps from partial-sky observations. The method combines regional processing with a hybrid design, utilizing standard convolution and dilated convolution to do a multiscale feature integration. We evaluate performance at both the map and power spectrum level using two masking scenarios: a generated random mask and the Planck 2018 common polarization inpainting mask. For both masking scenarios, SkyReconNet-P reproduces the large-scale morphology of the target maps. In power-spectrum space, we find that the reconstructed $E$-mode spectrum closely tracks the target at low multipoles, while small biases emerge at higher $\ell$. For $B$-mode, the raw reconstructed spectra exhibit a larger multipole-dependent bias, which we mitigate using a simulation-based linear calibration. We show that the calibrated $B$-mode spectrum preserve more information by comparing it with spectrum estimation using pseudo-$C_\ell$. Finally, we demonstrate cosmological parameter inference from calibrated reconstructed spectra by fitting $(r, A_{\rm lens})$ with a Gaussian bandpower likelihood, recovering posteriors consistent with injected parameters across three test ensembles down to $r \sim 10^{-3}$. These results support inpainting as a complementary route to cut-sky approaches when downstream pipelines can greatly benefit from statistically well-characterized, gap-filled polarization maps.

AI.tldr: SkyReconNet-P is a CNN-based method for inpainting CMB polarization maps that addresses foreground masking and incomplete sky coverage issues, enabling improved E/B separation and primordial B-mode searches through joint reconstruction of Q/U maps with multiscale feature integration.
AI.motivation: Foreground masking and incomplete sky coverage in CMB polarization analyses cause mode coupling and imperfect E/B separation, particularly impacting searches for primordial B-modes, necessitating effective inpainting methods to reconstruct missing polarization information.
AI.method: SkyReconNet-P extends the SkyReconNet framework using a convolutional neural network with regional processing and hybrid design combining standard and dilated convolutions for multiscale feature integration to jointly reconstruct polarization (Q,U) maps from partial-sky observations.
AI.result: The method successfully reproduces large-scale morphology of target maps for both random and Planck masks. E-mode spectra track targets at low multipoles with small biases at higher ℓ. B-mode spectra require simulation-based linear calibration to mitigate multipole-dependent biases, preserving more information than pseudo-Cℓ methods. Cosmological parameter inference (r, A_lens) recovers consistent posteriors down to r ∼ 10⁻³.
AI.conclusion: SkyReconNet-P demonstrates inpainting as a complementary approach to cut-sky methods, providing statistically well-characterized, gap-filled polarization maps that benefit downstream analysis pipelines, particularly for primordial B-mode searches and cosmological parameter inference.

title: Bayesian Cosmic Void Finding with Graph Flows
summary: Cosmic voids contain higher-order cosmological information and are of interest for astroparticle physics. Finding genuine matter underdensities in sparse galaxy surveys is, however, an underconstrained problem. Traditional void finding algorithms produce deterministic void catalogs, neglecting the probabilistic nature of the problem. We present a method to sample from the stochastic mapping from galaxy catalogs to arbitrary void definitions. Our algorithm uses a deep graph neural network to evolve "test particles" according to a flow-matching objective. We demonstrate the method in a simplified example setting but outline steps to generalize it towards practically usable void finders. Trained on a deterministic teacher, the model performs well but has considerable stochasticity which we interpret as regularization. Cosmological information in the predicted void catalogs outperforms the teacher. On the one hand, our method can cheaply emulate existing void finders with apparently useful regularization. More importantly, it also allows us to find the Bayes-optimal mapping between observed galaxies and any void definition. This includes definitions operating at the level of simulated matter density and velocity fields.

AI.tldr: A method using deep graph neural networks to sample from the stochastic mapping between galaxy catalogs and void definitions, enabling probabilistic void finding that outperforms deterministic approaches.
AI.motivation: Cosmic voids contain valuable cosmological information but finding genuine matter underdensities in sparse galaxy surveys is underconstrained. Traditional void finders produce deterministic catalogs, ignoring the inherent probabilistic nature of the problem.
AI.method: Uses a deep graph neural network to evolve "test particles" according to a flow-matching objective. The method samples from the stochastic mapping between galaxy catalogs and arbitrary void definitions, trained on a deterministic teacher but with inherent stochasticity.
AI.result: The model performs well with considerable stochasticity interpreted as regularization. Cosmological information in predicted void catalogs outperforms the deterministic teacher. The method can cheaply emulate existing void finders and find Bayes-optimal mappings between observed galaxies and void definitions.
AI.conclusion: The approach enables probabilistic void finding that captures inherent uncertainties, outperforms deterministic methods, and allows finding optimal mappings between observations and void definitions, including those based on simulated matter density and velocity fields.

title: Revising the Milky Way Cepheid Calibration: Quantifying and Correcting for Previously Undetected Distance Modulus Errors in the Gaia-based Multi-Wavelength Period-Luminosity Relations
summary: We examine the multi-wavelength period-luminosity-color relations for Cepheid variables in the Large and Small magellanic Clouds and the Milky Way. From first-principles stellar physics, the luminosity of a Cepheid is determined by its radius and surface temperature, yielding a fundamental PLC relation whose observational proxies are pulsation period and intrinsic color. Using Cepheids in the Magellanic Clouds, we show that the PLC relation recovers the known geometries and line-of-sight tilts of their disks, confirming its ability to detect true distance-modulus variations that are achromatic and consistent across all filters. Surprisingly, for Milky Way Cepheids with individually determined reddenings and HST and Gaia parallaxes, the residuals from multi-wavelength PL fits are also found to be achromatic, identical in sign and amplitude across all passbands, in this case indicating that parallax errors are the dominant source of scatter. Applying bandpass-averaged corrections to individual Cepheids recovers the theoretically expected wavelength-dependent narrowing of the instability strip, and results in revised parallaxes with a median improvement in precision of roughly a factor of two. In addition, they show no statistically significant correlation with metallicity over the range -0.2 < Fe/H < 0.05 dex. The final extinction- and reddening-corrected PLC relation yields an rms scatter of 0.04 mag, corresponding to 2 percent precision in distance per star. Use of a physically grounded PLC will provide a more robust foundation for the Cepheid-based extragalactic distance scale and the determination of the Hubble constant.

AI.tldr: The paper demonstrates that a physically-grounded period-luminosity-color (PLC) relation for Cepheid variables, derived from stellar physics principles, provides more accurate distance measurements with 2% precision per star and reduces scatter by correcting for achromatic systematic errors.
AI.motivation: To establish a more robust foundation for the Cepheid-based extragalactic distance scale and Hubble constant determination by moving beyond simple period-luminosity relations to a physically motivated period-luminosity-color relation that accounts for fundamental stellar properties.
AI.method: Analyzed multi-wavelength PLC relations for Cepheids in the Magellanic Clouds and Milky Way using first-principles stellar physics. Used Magellanic Cloud Cepheids to validate the PLC's ability to detect true distance variations, then applied bandpass-averaged corrections to individual Milky Way Cepheids with HST and Gaia parallaxes to recover wavelength-dependent instability strip narrowing.
AI.result: The PLC relation successfully recovered known geometries and tilts of Magellanic Cloud disks. For Milky Way Cepheids, residuals from PL fits were achromatic, indicating parallax errors as dominant scatter source. Applying corrections resulted in revised parallaxes with median precision improvement by factor of two, no significant metallicity correlation over -0.2 < Fe/H < 0.05 dex, and final extinction-corrected PLC relation with 0.04 mag rms scatter (2% distance precision per star).
AI.conclusion: A physically grounded PLC relation provides superior accuracy for Cepheid distance measurements, reduces systematic errors, and offers a more robust foundation for the extragalactic distance scale and Hubble constant determination compared to traditional period-luminosity relations.

title: Exploring Non-minimal coupling using ultra-diffuse galaxies
summary: We investigate whether a non-minimal coupling between dark matter and gravity can influence the internal dynamics of ultra-diffuse galaxies. Within this framework, the gravitational potential is modified by an additional term that captures the interaction between spacetime curvature and the dark matter with a coupling constant determined by a length scale $L$. Using spherical Jeans modeling, we analyze the kinematic data of three ultra-diffuse galaxies namely: NGC\;1052-DF2, NGC\;1052-DF4, and Dragonfly\;44, which span the observational extremes from dark matter deficient to dark matter dominated systems. For each galaxy we explore several dark matter halo profiles, two orbital anisotropy models, and both with and without Stellar-to-Halo Mass Relation scenarios, and we perform a Bayesian parameter inference. Our results show that across all the considered configurations, the constrained astrophysical parameters are consistent with standard ones from General Relativity. The posterior distributions of $L$ show no preference for non-zero values and result only in upper limits, suggesting that any non-minimal coupling contribution must be small and perturbative on this scales. Future high precision velocity measurements will be essential to determine whether non-minimal coupling effects can become observationally distinguishable in low-acceleration systems.

AI.tldr: Non-minimal coupling between dark matter and gravity shows no significant effects on ultra-diffuse galaxy dynamics, with only upper limits on coupling parameter L found across all tested configurations.
AI.motivation: Investigate whether non-minimal coupling between dark matter and gravity can influence internal dynamics of ultra-diffuse galaxies, particularly in systems spanning from dark matter deficient to dark matter dominated regimes.
AI.method: Used spherical Jeans modeling to analyze kinematic data of three ultra-diffuse galaxies (NGC 1052-DF2, NGC 1052-DF4, Dragonfly 44). Explored multiple dark matter halo profiles, orbital anisotropy models, with/without Stellar-to-Halo Mass Relation scenarios, and performed Bayesian parameter inference.
AI.result: Constrained astrophysical parameters consistent with standard General Relativity predictions. Posterior distributions of coupling parameter L show no preference for non-zero values, yielding only upper limits. Non-minimal coupling contributions must be small and perturbative on these scales.
AI.conclusion: Current data shows no evidence for non-minimal coupling effects in ultra-diffuse galaxy dynamics. Future high-precision velocity measurements needed to determine if such effects could become observable in low-acceleration systems.

title: Surveying the Giant HII Regions of the Milky Way with SOFIA: VIII. W43 Main
comment: 43 pages, 23 compressed figures, accepted for publication in ApJ. Version with full resolution images available at https://www.jim-debuizer.net/research-articles/
summary: In this eighth paper of the SOFIA-FORCAST series on Milky Way GHII regions, we present an analysis of the massive star-forming complex W43 Main. We compared our 11 - 37 micron maps with multi-wavelength observations from the near-infrared to radio, and investigated the physical nature of compact sources and dust substructures. We applied SED fitting to constrain properties of the compact infrared objects, and examined the evolutionary states of the extended subregions. We identified 20 compact infrared objects, 16 (80%) of which we classify as massive young stellar objects (MYSOs) or candidate MYSOs. W43 Main resides at the junction of the Scutum spiral arm and the Galactic Bar, a location where enhanced turbulence is anticipated and has been proposed as a potential influence on star-formation activity. Nevertheless, our analysis shows that its Lyman continuum photon production rate, the mass of its most massive MYSO, and its MYSO density are all consistent with the survey-wide median values. We therefore conclude that, despite W43 Main's unique Galactic environment, its present star formation activity appears broadly consistent with that of an average Galactic GHII region.

AI.tldr: W43 Main, a massive star-forming complex at the Galactic Bar-Scutum arm junction, shows star formation activity consistent with average Galactic GHII regions despite its unique turbulent environment.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether W43 Main's unique location at the junction of the Scutum spiral arm and Galactic Bar, where enhanced turbulence is expected, influences its star formation activity compared to other Galactic GHII regions.
AI.method: Multi-wavelength analysis combining SOFIA-FORCAST 11-37 micron maps with near-infrared to radio observations; SED fitting to constrain compact source properties; classification of infrared objects and examination of extended subregions' evolutionary states.
AI.result: Identified 20 compact infrared objects, with 16 (80%) classified as massive young stellar objects (MYSOs) or candidate MYSOs; found that Lyman continuum photon production rate, mass of most massive MYSO, and MYSO density are consistent with survey-wide median values.
AI.conclusion: Despite W43 Main's unique Galactic environment at a turbulent spiral arm-bar junction, its present star formation activity appears broadly consistent with that of an average Galactic GHII region.

title: The impact of the formation channel on gravitational-wave-galaxy cross-correlations
summary: The angular, harmonic cross-correlation between gravitational wave (GW) events and galaxy catalogues contains rich information on the large-scale structure and the origin of compact binary mergers. In this work, we study how uncertainties in the binary formation channel affect the predicted cross-correlation signal for both current-generation and next-generation networks of detectors. We generate five mock GW catalogues for which we vary the progenitor-to-remnant mass-transfer function and the time-delay probability distribution between progenitor and remnant. We then cross-correlate these catalogues with galaxy samples modelled on the 2MASS Photometric Redshift catalogue (2MPZ) and the Gaia-unWISE quasar catalogue (Quaia). We find that the mass-transfer function has negligible effect on the cross-correlation signal, with differences remaining within redshift uncertainties. In contrast, the time-delay distribution dramatically affects the redshift distribution of the GW events and, with it, the cross-correlation signal, particularly for shallow galaxy catalogues. In particular, current-generation facilities can achieve significant detections only for the longest time delays when cross-correlated with 2MPZ, whilst all cross-correlations with the deeper Quaia catalogue are marginally detectable or consistent with zero. Our exploratory results thus demonstrate that forecasts on cosmological or astrophysical parameters derived from GW-galaxy cross-correlations are, as expected, strongly sensitive to the assumed binary formation history.

AI.tldr: GW-galaxy cross-correlation signals are strongly affected by binary formation time delays but not by mass-transfer functions, with detection prospects varying significantly between current and next-generation detectors and different galaxy catalogues.
AI.motivation: To understand how uncertainties in binary formation channels (mass-transfer functions and time-delay distributions) affect predicted gravitational wave-galaxy cross-correlation signals for current and future detector networks.
AI.method: Generated five mock GW catalogues varying progenitor-to-remnant mass-transfer functions and time-delay probability distributions, then cross-correlated these with galaxy samples modelled on 2MPZ and Quaia catalogues.
AI.result: Mass-transfer functions have negligible effect on cross-correlation signals (differences within redshift uncertainties), while time-delay distributions dramatically affect GW redshift distributions and cross-correlation signals, particularly for shallow galaxy catalogues. Current-generation detectors achieve significant detections only for longest time delays with 2MPZ, while all cross-correlations with deeper Quaia catalogue are marginally detectable or consistent with zero.
AI.conclusion: Forecasts on cosmological or astrophysical parameters derived from GW-galaxy cross-correlations are strongly sensitive to assumed binary formation history, particularly time-delay distributions, highlighting the importance of understanding binary formation channels for accurate cosmological inference.

title: New Dynamical Measurements from a Lensed Quasar Sample: Joint Analysis Constrains the Mass Profile Evolution of Lens Galaxies
summary: We present a systematic study of the internal mass structure of early-type galaxies (ETGs) based on 106 galaxy-scale strong gravitational lenses with background quasars, all having spectroscopic redshifts. From this parent sample, we select 24 systems with high-quality ancillary data for joint analysis of strong lensing geometry and stellar kinematics. A key contribution is the derivation of new single-aperture stellar velocity dispersions for 11 lens galaxies via an iterative spectroscopic fitting procedure that mitigates quasar contamination, providing previously unavailable data. We model the total mass-density profile as a power law, $ρ\propto r^{-γ}$, and parameterise its logarithmic slope as $γ= γ_0 + γ_z \cdot z_l + γ_s \cdot \log \tildeΣ$, where $z_l$ is the lens redshift and $\tildeΣ$ the surface mass density. Within a flat $Λ$CDM framework and using DESI BAO measurements as a prior, we constrain the parameters via Monte Carlo nested sampling to $γ_0 = 1.62^{+0.11}_{-0.12}$, $γ_z = -0.35^{+0.08}_{-0.09}$, and $γ_s = 0.37^{+0.08}_{-0.07}$ ($68\%$ confidence intervals). Our results robustly demonstrate that $γ$ increases with surface mass density ($γ_s > 0$) and decreases with redshift ($γ_z < 0$). This implies that, at fixed redshift, galaxies with denser stellar cores have steeper mass profiles, while at fixed density, profiles become shallower at higher redshifts. By successfully applying the joint lensing--dynamics method to a substantial, independently acquired sample of lensed quasars, this work provides crucial validation of structural trends previously observed in galaxy--galaxy lensing systems, reinforcing the established evolutionary picture for massive ETGs and establishing lensed quasars as a potent probe of galaxy structure.

AI.tldr: Study of 106 strong-lens ETGs with background quasars reveals mass-density profile slopes depend on surface density (steeper for denser cores) and redshift (shallower at higher z), validating evolutionary trends in massive galaxies.
AI.motivation: To systematically investigate the internal mass structure of early-type galaxies using strong gravitational lensing with background quasars, and to validate previously observed structural trends from galaxy-galaxy lensing systems using an independent sample of lensed quasars.
AI.method: Analyzed 106 galaxy-scale strong gravitational lenses with background quasars (all with spectroscopic redshifts), selecting 24 systems with high-quality data for joint strong lensing geometry and stellar kinematics analysis. Derived new single-aperture stellar velocity dispersions for 11 lens galaxies using iterative spectroscopic fitting to mitigate quasar contamination. Modeled total mass-density profile as power law ρ∝r^{-γ} with parameterization γ = γ₀ + γ_z·z_l + γ_s·logΣ̃. Constrained parameters using Monte Carlo nested sampling within flat ΛCDM framework with DESI BAO measurements as prior.
AI.result: Constrained parameters to γ₀ = 1.62^{+0.11}_{-0.12}, γ_z = -0.35^{+0.08}_{-0.09}, and γ_s = 0.37^{+0.08}_{-0.07} (68% confidence). Robustly demonstrated that mass-density slope γ increases with surface mass density (γ_s > 0) and decreases with redshift (γ_z < 0). At fixed redshift, galaxies with denser stellar cores have steeper mass profiles; at fixed density, profiles become shallower at higher redshifts.
AI.conclusion: The study successfully applies joint lensing-dynamics method to a substantial, independently acquired sample of lensed quasars, providing crucial validation of structural trends previously observed in galaxy-galaxy lensing systems. This reinforces the established evolutionary picture for massive early-type galaxies and establishes lensed quasars as a potent probe of galaxy structure.

title: Multiwavelength Characterization of a Dynamically Relaxed Cool Core Galaxy Cluster at $z=1.5$
comment: 17 pages, 9 figures, 1 table. Accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: We present imaging and spectroscopic analyses of Chandra and XMM-Newton observations of ACT-CL J0123.5$-$0428, one of the most massive, highest redshift galaxy clusters detected within the survey fields of the Atacama Cosmology Telescope. The Chandra data are sufficient to characterize the morphology of this cluster and constrain the geometrically deprojected temperature in 2 spatial bins out to $r_{2500}$, revealing a dynamically relaxed system whose temperature drops to $kT = 1.8\pm0.6$ keV in the inner $\sim40$kpc. Within this same inner radius, the surface brightness and density of the ICM is sharply peaked, and the cooling time falls to $t_\mathrm{cool}=280^{+150}_{-120}$ Myr. A novel forward-modeling analysis of the XMM data extends imaging and spectroscopic measurements of this system out to $r_{500}$, constraining the redshift to $z=1.50\pm0.03$, with a mean temperature of $kT = 7.3\pm1.1$ keV and an emission-weighted mean metallicity of $Z/Z_\odot = 0.43^{+0.46}_{-0.25}$. We also utilize the limited optical/IR photometric coverage of the cluster to characterize the properties of the brightest cluster galaxy (BCG), which is coincident with the X-ray peak. Despite the high redshift and strong cool core, the BCG exhibits no signs of recent or ongoing star formation, suggesting AGN feedback has been acting persistently to stem star formation since $z\sim 2.5$. These measurements identify ACT-CL J0123.5$-$0428 as the highest redshift, dynamically relaxed, cool core galaxy cluster discovered to date, making it a premier target for future astrophysical and cosmological studies.

AI.tldr: ACT-CL J0123.5-0428 is the highest redshift (z=1.50) dynamically relaxed cool core galaxy cluster discovered to date, characterized by X-ray observations showing a strong cool core with low central temperature (1.8 keV) and short cooling time (280 Myr), despite no signs of star formation in the BCG.
AI.motivation: To characterize one of the most massive, highest redshift galaxy clusters detected by the Atacama Cosmology Telescope, specifically analyzing its thermodynamic properties, dynamical state, and the relationship between its cool core and brightest cluster galaxy to understand AGN feedback mechanisms in high-redshift clusters.
AI.method: Combined imaging and spectroscopic analyses using Chandra and XMM-Newton observations. Chandra data used for morphology characterization and geometrically deprojected temperature measurements in 2 spatial bins out to r_2500. XMM data analyzed with novel forward-modeling to extend measurements to r_500, constraining redshift, mean temperature, and metallicity. Limited optical/IR photometric coverage used to analyze the brightest cluster galaxy properties.
AI.result: The cluster is dynamically relaxed with a strong cool core: inner ~40 kpc temperature drops to 1.8±0.6 keV, cooling time falls to 280^{+150}_{-120} Myr, and ICM density is sharply peaked. Redshift constrained to z=1.50±0.03, mean temperature 7.3±1.1 keV, emission-weighted metallicity Z/Z_⊙ = 0.43^{+0.46}_{-0.25}. Despite the strong cool core, the BCG shows no signs of recent or ongoing star formation, suggesting persistent AGN feedback since z~2.5.
AI.conclusion: ACT-CL J0123.5-0428 is the highest redshift, dynamically relaxed, cool core galaxy cluster discovered to date, making it a premier target for future astrophysical and cosmological studies. The lack of star formation in the BCG despite the strong cool core indicates effective AGN feedback has been operating since z~2.5.

title: Modelling the non-equilibrium chemistry of the Milky Way's cold nuclear wind
comment: 18 pages, 7 figures, 4 tables. Submitted for publication in MNRAS
summary: Cold atomic and molecular gas are commonly observed in the winds of both external galaxies and the Milky Way, yet the survival and origin of these cool phases within hot galactic winds is poorly understood. To help gain insight into these problems, we carry out time-dependent chemical modelling of cool clouds in the Milky Way's nuclear wind, which possess unusual molecularto-atomic hydrogen ratios that are inconsistent with both disc values and predictions from chemical equilibrium models. We confirm that CO and Hi emission comparable to that in the observed nuclear wind clouds cannot be produced by gas in chemical equilibrium, but that such conditions can be produced in a molecule-dominated cloud that has had its atomic envelope rapidly removed and has not yet reached a new chemical equilibrium. Clouds in this state harbour large reservoirs of molecular gas and consequently have anomalously large CO-to-H2 conversion factors, suggesting that the masses of the observed clouds may be significantly larger than suggested by earlier analyses assuming disc-like conversions. These findings provide a new framework for interpreting cold gas in galactic winds, providing strong evidence that cold outflows can originate from the galactic disc molecular clouds that survive acceleration into the wind but lose their diffuse atomic envelopes in the process, and suggesting that the Milky Way's nuclear outflow may be more heavily mass-loaded than previously thought.

AI.tldr: Cold gas in galactic winds survives via molecular clouds losing their atomic envelopes during acceleration, explaining anomalous molecular-to-atomic ratios and requiring revised mass estimates.
AI.motivation: To understand the survival and origin of cold atomic and molecular gas in hot galactic winds, particularly explaining unusual molecular-to-atomic hydrogen ratios observed in Milky Way's nuclear wind clouds that contradict both disc values and chemical equilibrium predictions.
AI.method: Time-dependent chemical modeling of cool clouds in the Milky Way's nuclear wind, analyzing non-equilibrium chemical states after rapid removal of atomic envelopes.
AI.result: Observed CO and Hi emission cannot be produced by gas in chemical equilibrium but can be explained by molecule-dominated clouds that have lost their atomic envelopes and are not yet in new equilibrium. These clouds have large molecular reservoirs and anomalously high CO-to-H2 conversion factors, indicating cloud masses may be significantly larger than previous estimates.
AI.conclusion: Cold outflows originate from galactic disc molecular clouds that survive acceleration into winds but lose their diffuse atomic envelopes, suggesting the Milky Way's nuclear outflow is more heavily mass-loaded than previously thought and providing a new framework for interpreting cold gas in galactic winds.

title: Improved frequency hierarchy treatment for anisotropic spectral distortions
comment: 36 pages, 6 figures, to be submitted to JCAP, comments welcome!
summary: Spectral distortion anisotropies of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) provide a new probe of the early Universe that can be accessed using traditional CMB imaging techniques. It is possible to compute the creation and evolution of anisotropic signals for various scenarios using the frequency hierarchy method recently developed for CosmoTherm. However, the current treatment is not perfect and some approximations had to be made. Here, we carefully construct a modified form for the evolution equations that has the full equilibrium solutions built into the formulation. We improve the formalism to account for i) additional stimulated scattering effects, ii) kinematic corrections to the thermalization terms, iii) corrections to the standard perturbation variables and iv) direct photon sources. These effect could not be captured with the original formulation of the frequency hierarchy method but are indeed important for cleanly separating real distortions from temperature signals. However, we show that previous results are not altered significantly when compared to the improved formulation presented here. As a new worked example, which could indeed not be treated before, we also illustrate how possible changes in the temperature-redshift relation would create spectral distortion anisotropies in the pre-recombination era. The theoretical methods presented here are also an important step towards being able to consistently predict the CMB spectral distortion anisotropies in photon-dark photon and photon-axion conversion scenarios.

AI.tldr: Improved formalism for CMB spectral distortion anisotropies using modified frequency hierarchy method with full equilibrium solutions, addressing stimulated scattering, kinematic corrections, perturbation variables, and direct photon sources.
AI.motivation: Current treatment of CMB spectral distortion anisotropies using frequency hierarchy method has approximations and lacks full equilibrium solutions, limiting accurate separation of real distortions from temperature signals and preventing treatment of certain scenarios like temperature-redshift relation changes.
AI.method: Modified evolution equations with full equilibrium solutions built into formulation, improving formalism to account for: i) additional stimulated scattering effects, ii) kinematic corrections to thermalization terms, iii) corrections to standard perturbation variables, and iv) direct photon sources.
AI.result: Previous results not significantly altered by improved formulation, but new scenarios can now be treated, such as temperature-redshift relation changes creating spectral distortion anisotropies in pre-recombination era.
AI.conclusion: Improved theoretical methods enable consistent prediction of CMB spectral distortion anisotropies for previously untreatable scenarios, including photon-dark photon and photon-axion conversion scenarios, advancing early Universe probes.

title: Dense Molecular Clumps with Large Blue Asymmetries: Evidence for Collapse
summary: An analysis of the Millimetre Astronomy Legacy Team 90 GHz (MALT90) survey has produced a sample of 27 candidate dense molecular clumps with large collapse motions, as revealed by large ``blue'' asymmetrical line profiles of the optically thick \hcop\, line. %with respect to the optically thin \nthp\, line. New, more sensitive molecular line observations of this sample, conducted with the Mopra 22-m telescope, confirm the blue asymmetries in the \hcop\, line profiles, with large, positive values of the asymmetry parameter $A$ ($\bar{A}_{HCO^+} = 0.69\pm0.01$), and positive, but smaller asymmetries in the \hcn\, and \hnc\, lines: ($\bar{A}_{HCN} = 0.35\pm0.01$ and $\bar{A}_{HNC} = 0.28\pm0.01$), as expected for a less optically thick tracer in collapsing clumps. The small, positive mean asymmetry parameters for \cch\, and \htcop, $\bar{A}_{C_2H} = 0.15\pm0.02$ and $\bar{A}_{H^{13}CO^+} = 0.18\pm0.03$, likely indicate slightly optically thick emission for at least some clumps. The hyperfine ratios for \nthp\, are in their optically thin, LTE, values, but for \hcn\ they are not; the $F=1 \to 1$ hyperfine line shows abnormally weak intensities. A simple two-component model shows that self-absorption of the background $F = 1 \to 1$ hyperfine line by the main $F = 2 \to 1$ hyperfine line of a cold, foreground, redshifted cloud can reproduce the observed \hcn\, hyperfine intensities and match the \hcn\, and \hcop\, line profiles. All of these results are consistent with self-absorption of the optically thick lines on the red side of the profile, as expected for collapsing clumps. A simple two-cloud model suggests that this sample represents dense clumps with extreme collapse velocities, $V_{inf} \sim 2.4$ \kms.

AI.tldr: Analysis of MALT90 survey identifies 27 dense molecular clumps with blue asymmetric line profiles indicating collapse motions, confirmed by Mopra observations showing large asymmetries in HCO+ and smaller asymmetries in HCN/HNC, consistent with self-absorption in collapsing clumps with extreme velocities ~2.4 km/s.
AI.motivation: To identify and characterize dense molecular clumps undergoing gravitational collapse by analyzing asymmetric line profiles from the MALT90 survey, which can reveal infall motions in star-forming regions.
AI.method: Analyzed MALT90 survey data to identify candidate clumps with blue asymmetries in HCO+ line profiles, then conducted follow-up observations with Mopra 22-m telescope of HCO+, HCN, HNC, C2H, and H13CO+ lines. Used asymmetry parameter A to quantify line profile asymmetries and developed two-component models to interpret hyperfine line ratios and self-absorption effects.
AI.result: Confirmed blue asymmetries in HCO+ (Ā = 0.69±0.01), with smaller asymmetries in HCN (0.35±0.01) and HNC (0.28±0.01). C2H and H13CO+ showed small positive asymmetries (0.15±0.02 and 0.18±0.03). HCN hyperfine ratios showed abnormal F=1→1 line weakness explained by self-absorption. All results consistent with self-absorption on red side of profiles in collapsing clumps with extreme collapse velocities ~2.4 km/s.
AI.conclusion: The sample represents dense molecular clumps undergoing extreme gravitational collapse with velocities ~2.4 km/s, as evidenced by blue asymmetric line profiles and self-absorption effects in optically thick tracers, providing observational evidence for advanced stages of star formation.

title: Gravitational Wave Echoes of the First Order Phase Transition in a Kination-Induced Big Bang
summary: Gravitational waves (GWs) produced during first-order phase transitions (FOPTs) in the early universe provide a powerful probe of nonstandard cosmological histories. We study GW production from a FOPT ending a kination-dominated epoch in the Kination-Induced Big Bang scenario, in which a period of kination domination terminates through a phase transition that reheats the universe into radiation domination. A rolling scalar field drives the kination epoch. In the specific model we consider, its derivative coupling to a second scalar (tunneling field) dynamically traps the latter in a false vacuum, with the phase transition triggered as the kination field slows due to Hubble friction. We compute the resulting stochastic GW background from bubble nucleation and collisions, presenting analytic estimates and numerical results for the peak amplitude and frequency. In all cases we find an upper bound $Ω_{\rm GW} h^2\lesssim 2\times10^{-7}$ from the bubble percolation condition. In the case where the false vacuum energy dominates at the transition (yet the kination field drives the FOPT), we find $Ω_{\rm GW}h^2\gtrsim 10^{-12}$. We further find that the Hubble scale during the phase transition across a broad set of model parameters is bounded by $\mathscr{O}(10^{-13})M^2/M_{\rm Pl}\lesssim H_* \lesssim \mathscr{O}(0.1)M^2/M_{\rm Pl}$, where $M$ is the mass-scale controlling the strength of the interaction between the kination and tunneling fields. The predicted signal spans frequencies from nHz to MHz, allowing the model to explain the signal reported by Pulsar Timing Array experiments and to be constrained or probed by interferometers such as LISA, Advanced LIGO, Cosmic Explorer, and BBO. Interestingly, a FOPT can occur even if the bare tunneling potential has a single minimum, as metastability is generated dynamically by the coupling between the tunneling and the kination field.

AI.tldr: GWs from FOPTs ending kination domination in Kination-Induced Big Bang scenario, with analytic/numerical predictions for GW background amplitude/frequency, applicable to PTA signals and future interferometers.
AI.motivation: GWs from FOPTs probe nonstandard cosmological histories; study GW production from FOPT ending kination-dominated epoch in Kination-Induced Big Bang scenario to understand early universe dynamics and connect to observable GW signals.
AI.method: Model with rolling scalar field driving kination epoch, derivative-coupled to tunneling field that gets dynamically trapped in false vacuum; compute stochastic GW background from bubble nucleation/collisions using analytic estimates and numerical calculations.
AI.result: Upper bound Ω_GW h² ≲ 2×10⁻⁷ from bubble percolation; for false vacuum energy dominated transitions, Ω_GW h² ≳ 10⁻¹²; Hubble scale bounded by O(10⁻¹³)M²/M_Pl ≲ H_* ≲ O(0.1)M²/M_Pl; signal spans nHz-MHz frequencies.
AI.conclusion: FOPTs can occur even with single-minimum bare tunneling potential due to dynamical metastability; predicted GW signals can explain PTA observations and be probed by current/future interferometers, providing constraints on kination-induced phase transitions.

title: Effective Magnetic Susceptibility of Dust Grains with Superparamagnetic Inclusions and Implications
comment: 17 pages, 5 figures. To be submitted to AAS journals in a week. Comments are welcome
summary: Magnetic properties of dust grains play a fundamental role in their alignment with ambient magnetic fields and magnetic dipole emission. In the radiative torque (RAT) paradigm, superparamagnetic inclusions (SPIs) embedded within dust grains are expected to significantly enhance magnetic susceptibility and alignment efficiency. Previous studies have generally assumed SPIs of a single characteristic size. In this work, we develop an effective superparamagnetism model that explicitly accounts for a power-law size distribution of SPIs. We show that the effective zero-frequency susceptibility can be described by the superparamagnetic susceptibility of uniform-sized inclusions evaluated at the critical blocking size, reduced by a factor $F_{\rm eff}\sim 0.1$. It exhibits a slight increase with dust temperature $T_{d}$, in contrast to the rapid decrease for the case of single-size SPIs. For rotating grains at angular frequency $ω$, we identify a characteristic resonance size of SPIs that dominates the magnetic response, $N_{\rm res} = (T_{d}/T_{\rm act}) \ln (ν_{0}/ω)$ with $T_{\rm act}$ activation temperature and $ν_{0}$ the characteristic attempt frequency of SPIs. The frequency-dependent effective susceptibility is well described by the maximum susceptibility $χ_{\rm eff}^{\rm max}(ω)$ at $N_{\rm res}$, reduced by a factor $G_{\rm eff}\sim 0.1$. Unlike models assuming uniform-sized inclusions, we find that the effective susceptibility exhibits a nearly flat spectrum for frequency below $ν_{0}$, arising from the progressive activation of larger inclusions at lower frequencies. This effective superparamagnetism model based on the SPI size distrbution has important implications for magnetic grain alignment, dust polarization, and magnetic dipole emission across diverse environments.

AI.tldr: Develops an effective superparamagnetism model accounting for power-law size distribution of superparamagnetic inclusions (SPIs) in dust grains, showing how size distribution affects magnetic susceptibility and alignment efficiency compared to single-size SPI models.
AI.motivation: Previous studies assumed single characteristic size for superparamagnetic inclusions (SPIs) in dust grains, but realistic SPI populations follow size distributions. This oversimplification may lead to inaccurate predictions of magnetic susceptibility, grain alignment, and magnetic dipole emission in the radiative torque (RAT) paradigm.
AI.method: Develops an effective superparamagnetism model that explicitly incorporates a power-law size distribution of SPIs. Derives analytical expressions for zero-frequency susceptibility and frequency-dependent susceptibility, identifying characteristic resonance size of SPIs that dominates magnetic response based on dust temperature and grain rotation frequency.
AI.result: Effective zero-frequency susceptibility can be described by superparamagnetic susceptibility of uniform-sized inclusions evaluated at critical blocking size, reduced by factor F_eff ~ 0.1. It shows slight increase with dust temperature T_d, contrasting rapid decrease for single-size SPIs. Frequency-dependent susceptibility exhibits nearly flat spectrum below characteristic attempt frequency ν_0 due to progressive activation of larger inclusions at lower frequencies.
AI.conclusion: The effective superparamagnetism model based on SPI size distribution provides more realistic predictions of magnetic properties, with important implications for magnetic grain alignment, dust polarization, and magnetic dipole emission across diverse astrophysical environments.

title: Prospects of Indirect Detection of Dark Matter via Primordial Black Hole Induced Gravitational Waves
summary: Primordial black holes (PBHs), produced in the early Universe, can source a stochastic background of induced gravitational waves (GWs) and provide a non-thermal origin for dark matter (DM). We investigate DM production in a PBH-dominated cosmological framework, including contributions from PBH evaporation, gravitational production, and thermal freeze-in and freeze-out mechanisms, and determine the regions consistent with the observed DM relic abundance. We find that thermal freeze-in can compensate for the underabundance of PBH-sourced DM, while indirect detection remains largely insensitive due to the feeble interaction strength, making future GW observatories such as LISA and the Einstein Telescope (ET) unique probes of this scenario. For freeze-out DM, indirect detection experiments constrain regions with relatively large annihilation cross-sections, whereas GW observations probe complementary regions with heavier DM masses and smaller interaction strengths. Consequently, the same DM parameter space cannot be simultaneously probed by both indirect detection searches and GW missions. These results establish GW observations as a powerful and independent probe of DM production in PBH-dominated cosmologies, opening a new observational window into DM properties and the thermal history of the pre-BBN Universe.

AI.tldr: PBHs can produce DM via multiple mechanisms; GW observations from LISA/ET uniquely probe this scenario, complementing but not overlapping with indirect detection constraints.
AI.motivation: To investigate dark matter production in PBH-dominated cosmologies and determine observational signatures, particularly how gravitational wave observations can probe DM properties that are inaccessible to traditional indirect detection methods.
AI.method: Analyze DM production through four mechanisms in PBH-dominated framework: PBH evaporation, gravitational production, thermal freeze-in, and thermal freeze-out. Determine parameter regions consistent with observed DM relic abundance and assess detectability via GW observatories (LISA, ET) and indirect detection experiments.
AI.result: Thermal freeze-in can compensate for PBH-sourced DM underabundance; GW observations uniquely probe this scenario due to feeble interaction strengths. For freeze-out DM, indirect detection constrains regions with large annihilation cross-sections, while GW probes complementary regions with heavier DM masses and smaller interaction strengths. The two methods probe non-overlapping parameter spaces.
AI.conclusion: Gravitational wave observations from future missions like LISA and ET provide a powerful, independent probe of DM production in PBH-dominated cosmologies, offering a new observational window into DM properties and pre-BBN thermal history that complements but does not overlap with indirect detection methods.

title: Large-scale and local environmental drivers of quenching: tracing H$α$ concentration in X-ray and optical galaxy groups
comment: 20 pages, 19 figures. Submitted to MNRAS. Comments from referee addressed
